title: Why the First n Odd Numbers Sum to n²
summary: A one-page introduction to mathematical induction, geometric growth, and the Lean proof that adding the first n odd numbers produces an n by n square.
audience: Learners meeting proof by induction or Lean for the first time.

paper.title: Why Odd Numbers Build Perfect Squares

glossary.explanation: A natural number of the form 2k + 1. The sequence begins 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9.
A proof method with a base case and a successor step: prove the claim at zero, then prove that each established case gives the next one.
The natural number after n, written n + 1. Lean exposes this as the second branch of the inductive proof.

mappings.label: Build the sum one odd number at a time
mappings.correspondenceNote: The recursive Lean definition states exactly the paper's running-sum step: the sum at n + 1 is the previous sum plus 2n + 1.

mappings.label: The first n odd numbers sum to n²

paper.heading: Theorem
paper.quote: For every natural number n, the sum of the first n odd numbers is n².

mappings.correspondenceNote: The Lean theorem follows the same base-and-successor structure as the paper. Its final simplification is the algebraic square-growth step shown in the displayed equation.

mappings.label: A square grows by the next odd number

paper.heading: Why the algebra matches the picture
